findings.text: The error message interpolates the rejected value with a template literal. A Symbol or a null-prototype object, such as `Object.create(null)`, makes the template literal throw its own 'Cannot convert ... to a string' TypeError. The caller then sees that message instead of the intended '<name> must be a string or a file URL'.

0.reason: Interpolating a Symbol or a null-prototype object in the template literal at file-url.js:13 throws its own TypeError ('Cannot convert a Symbol value to a string' or 'Cannot convert object to primitive value') before the intended '<name> must be a string or a file URL' error is built; the input is still rejected but with a misleading message, and this has nothing to do with Deno's String-object execPath.
